product_boundaries.riAuth Essentials: OIDC/OAuth, passkeys, complete browser self-service, compact administration, groups and claims, API/CLI, audit, backups, LDAP import, and outbound SCIM.
product_boundaries.riAuth Platform: Essentials plus configurable workflows, broader protocols, advanced federation, cloud connectors, device integrations, and expanded administration.
product_boundaries.riauthctl: Remote administration, with optional terminal USB-authenticator support separated from the server.

shared_invariant: Both server builds retain the same identity, authorization, revocation, and credential-protection semantics for shared capabilities.

labels.preserve: Behavior exists, is regression-tested, and meets the item; the work is to keep it intact through refactors and lift its tests into shared contracts.
labels.extend: A meaningful implementation exists, but the item needs more surface, interfaces, or limits removed.
labels.build: Little or no implementation exists; the item needs new design and code.
labels.verify: An implementation exists; what is missing is acceptance evidence (conformance, real peers, tenants, hardware), not code.

journey_levels.module: An endpoint, module, or API exists; no complete user or operator journey.
journey_levels.partial: The journey completes, but only through some interfaces (for example terminal only) or with documented gaps.
journey_levels.complete-local: The complete journey is exercised by local tests or fixtures; real-peer evidence is still separate.
journey_levels.process: Process or documentation item; journey not applicable.

evidence_method.inspected: Source, tests, Cargo manifests, Dockerfile, CI and release workflows, scripts, deploy templates, and docs at the base revision; test names were extracted from #[test]/#[tokio::test] attributes

ci_meaning.ci-check: Selected by `cargo test --all-targets --features test-support,fuzzing` in the Public CI check job
ci_meaning.ci-integration (#[ignore], external prog: Run with --ignored in the Public CI integration job with the named external program
ci_meaning.not-in-ci: Present in the repository but not invoked by any workflow

not_verified: CI pass or fail status at the base revision (no network access used)
Contents or publication state of the v0.1.1 GitHub release
Any real-peer, tenant, hardware or conformance outcome

pipeline_smoke_checks: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md equality in image and tarball
libssl3t64 and libudev1 copyright files present

suggested_first_slice.summary: Test-only contract harness for INV-1..INV-4 parameterized over the Store backend (redb in the check job, PostgreSQL in the integration job) before A03 moves Store::security_transition

items.title: Verify SAML, LDAP, and RADIUS profiles
items.label: verify
items.current_state: SAML is checked against independent xmlsec1 (CI integration). LDAP sync runs against a real OpenLDAP (`scripts/test-ldap.sh`). RADIUS EAP-TLS is checked against the OpenSSL client. The LDAP provider and RADIUS RadSec use local fixtures. Loopback PAP was exercised with FreeRADIUS radclient 3.2.10 (`scripts/test-radius.sh`): a correct password returned Access-Accept and radclient exited 0, a wrong password returned Access-Reject and radclient exited 1, and an identical datagram returned the cached Access-Accept without another `radius.accept`. Loopback STARTTLS was exercised with OpenLDAP ldapsearch 2.7.1 (`scripts/test-ldap-provider.sh`): the service bind and page size 1 returned the two in-scope users on separate pages and ldapsearch exited 0, a disabled member was omitted, and a wrong token and a revoked agent each exited 49 with invalid credentials. The same ignored test bound a separate LDAPS listener at 127.0.0.1:60248 and STARTTLS at 127.0.0.1:60249. OpenLDAP ldapsearch 2.7.1 used `ldaps://127.0.0.1:60248` without `-ZZ` and `LDAPTLS_REQCERT=hard` against the fixture CA: page size 1 returned the two in-scope users and exited 0, a disabled member was omitted, a wrong token and a revoked agent each exited 49, and an unrelated CA exited 1 with `certificate verify failed (unable to get local issuer certificate)`. `ldaps://` on the STARTTLS port exited 1 with `Connect error (-11)`, and `ldap://` with `-ZZ` on the LDAPS port exited 1 with `ldap_start_tls: Can't contact LDAP server (-1)`. A loopback GNU Lasso 2.9.0 helper (Homebrew bottle 2.9.0_4; `pkg-config --modversion lasso` printed `2.9.0`; `liblasso.3.dylib` links xmlsec1 1.3.12) is `scripts/lasso-saml-sp.c`, run by ignored `tests/saml_sp_peer.rs::lasso_signed_redirect_request_post_response_signature_and_metadata_key` through `scripts/test-saml-sp.sh`. The helper signed an HTTP-Redirect AuthnRequest with `SigAlg` `http://www.w3.org/2001/04/xmldsig-more#rsa-sha256`, then accepted riAuth's HTTP-POST response and printed a persistent NameID with exit 0. Changing one NameID hex digit, and replacing every IdP metadata `X509Certificate`, each exited 1 with `Failed to verify signature. (-111)` and printed no NameID. `lasso_set_min_signature_method` is not exported, so the library minimum stays RSA-SHA1; verification stayed forced and the request still used RSA-SHA256. After signature verification, the helper requires `lasso_saml2_assertion_validate_audience` to be valid for its provider ID and `lasso_saml2_assertion_validate_time_checks` to be valid at the current time. The unmodified response still exited 0 and printed `signature: lasso`, `audience: lasso`, `lifetime: lasso`, `recipient: helper`, and a persistent NameID. Signature verification, `lasso_saml2_assertion_validate_audience`, and `lasso_saml2_assertion_validate_time_checks` are Lasso API checks. Lasso 2.9.0 does not compare Recipient; the helper compares it with the ACS URL from `lasso_provider_get_assertion_consumer_service_url`. Setting `Conditions` `NotOnOrAfter` to that element's `NotBefore` and re-signing with the same IdP key exited 1 with `lasso lifetime: assertion lifetime is not valid (1)`. Setting only `Recipient` to `https://sp.example.test/bad` and re-signing exited 1 with `helper recipient: assertion Recipient does not match the SP assertion consumer service`. Both re-signed failures printed no NameID, and neither stderr contained `(-111)`. The SP entity is the fixture `https://sp.example.test/metadata`. Named production service providers and supplicant peers remain unused.

items.title: Build operational dashboards and diagnostics
items.label: extend
items.current_state: Prometheus metrics, doctor, logout and mail delivery endpoints, an alert rules template, and an alert webhook remain. doctor counts users, clients, and logout deliveries one storage page of 128 at a time inside the same snapshot. The response fields and healthy rule are unchanged. Each page decodes full values, and this read does not size-cap a stored value. Platform GET /api/operations/offboarding (riauth offboard diagnostics) counts every scheduled-offboarding job and lists at most 50 redacted attention items: failed jobs, done jobs whose live downstream state is pending or incomplete, and scheduled or running jobs that already have last_error. Items and visible targets report has_error and leave the stored error text on the job read. operations.read on operations/offboarding sees the counts; an item also requires user.offboard on the stored username. Hidden targets still decide downstream state. affects_readiness is false, and doctor, /readyz, and /livez stay on their existing answers. deploy/riauth-grafana.json is a Grafana dashboard document for the PromQL in deploy/riauth-alerts.yml. scripts/check-grafana-dashboard.py checks that JSON and requires every PromQL metric name to be rendered by the process and present in those rules. The file has not been imported into Grafana. Request counters, the unlabeled request histogram, rate limits, worker rejections, and queue gauges are rendered in src/api/observability.rs. Signing errors, cleanup errors, and storage write wait are rendered in src/telemetry.rs. Each queue gauge is one series per queue label. pending and failed are index aggregates, and oldest pending age is the earliest timestamp in the pending age index. Connector lag, storage pressure, key problems, and readiness stay off this dashboard. Node mismatch remains O03. queues.offboard_jobs.failed still counts status failed only. Downstream resolved is an attestation. Failed provisioning jobs and mail deliveries stay on their existing reads. GET /api/operations/reconciliation counts stored reconciliation schedules and retained jobs and lists at most 50 redacted attention rows: failed jobs, stale jobs other than a schedule disabled before dispatch, queued or running jobs that already have last_error, and schedules that already have last_error. Items report has_error and a fixed next_action, and leave stored error text on the schedule and job reads. next_run is the next enqueue time, so this read does not measure connector lag. operations.read on operations/reconciliation sees every controller scope. affects_readiness is false. The offboarding read still scans offboard_jobs and does not add a Prometheus series. Platform GET /api/operations/offboarding/deactivations pages provisioning_deactivations at the storage page of 128, counts every stored deactivation, and retains at most 50 redacted attention rows for delivery states pending, failed, ambiguous, and dismissed. Job records are not read, and the response has no job-linkage field. Rows with no job record stay in the counts because the scan is the deactivation bucket. Each page decodes up to 128 full deactivation values, and this read does not size-cap a stored value. has_error and a fixed next_action leave stored error text, URLs, and remote identifiers on the deactivation read. An item requires user.offboard on the account's current username; the stored username is not the authorization key. A missing account is visible to a full administrator without that stored name, and an agent leaves it withheld. operations.read on operations/offboarding is required. affects_readiness is false. Essentials keeps GET /api/provisioning/deactivations and does not serve this route. riauth offboard diagnostics remains the job aggregate. GET /api/operations/mail already returns each row's id, timestamps, attempts, next attempt, delivered time, and stopped flag, and omits the recipient, subject, body, proof, and lease. No SMTP error string is stored. mail_deliveries pending, failed, and oldest pending age stay on metrics and Prometheus. Platform GET /api/operations/ssf pages ssf_deliveries at the storage page of 128, counts every stored outbound delivery, and retains at most 50 redacted attention rows for retrying, stopped, and cancelled. pending and delivered stay in the counts. A row with delivered_at is delivered. A stopped row with last_failed is stopped; a stopped row without last_failed is cancelled, including a deleted stream or an endpoint change, because this read does not load the stream record. event is account_disabled, session_revoked, credential_change, or unknown. The raw event string, endpoint, subject, audience, JTI, and credential type stay on the delivery record. An item requires ssf.configure or ssf.manage on ssf/<stored stream id>; other rows are withheld with no stream id. operations.read on operations/ssf is required. Each page decodes up to 128 full delivery values, and this read does not size-cap a stored value. affects_readiness is false. Essentials does not serve this route. queues.ssf_deliveries.failed still collapses retrying, stopped, and cancelled.

invariants_to_preserve.invariant: Disabling a user durably revokes child agents, Windows devices and tickets, queues RP logout and SSF; re-enable never restores them
Authentication proofs are single-use and bound to the request and session
One-time codes and tokens have exactly one winner; replay revokes the family
Prepared authentication revalidates revocation and authority before commit
Agents cannot create or modify administrators; the last administrator is preserved
Upstream identities never link by email or username; linking is explicit
Temporary grants never change durable membership
Policy is re-evaluated at refresh, userinfo and proxy, not only at issuance
Configuration rejects unknown keys (no silently ignored configuration)
Schema upgrades are atomic and future schema versions are refused
